correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact identity f(N[v_ij])=r_i+c_j-x_ij. A total below 2n yields a row and column both of sum at most one and hence an immediate lower-bound violation. At weight 2n, row sums zero and one are separately excluded by forced column lower bounds; symmetry then gives every row and column sum two. The converse checks every possible constrained entry exactly. The counting argument correctly identifies equality matrices with 2-regular bipartite multigraphs and accounts for the two alternating matching decompositions of each nontrivial cycle. The packaged verifier independently exhausts 662,647 bounded-weight labelings for n=2,3,4 and matches both the classification and coefficient formula.

value.rationale: Square rook graphs are canonical Cartesian products, Hamming graphs, and line graphs of complete bipartite graphs. The theorem gives a complete natural equality classification, not merely another scalar value: minimum functions are exactly integer transportation matrices with margins two. The optimizer family has an exact weighted-permutation count via 2-regular bipartite multigraphs, exposing a structural connection likely useful in extensions to rectangular or higher-dimensional product families.
